answer: One concrete defense is requiring each agent to stake a scarce deposit before it can transact. An identity locks copper tokens that are slashed if peers prove it created duplicates or faked work, so creating a thousand fake agents means funding a thousand deposits at risk. Newcomers also start on a low-trust knoll with narrow permissions and earn wider access only after verifiable behavior. A violet flag from an audit can freeze that progress, forcing the attacker to pay again. Honest agents keep their stake, while a Sybil operator faces a cost that grows linearly with every fake identity.
